newsitem.title: USA: New website shows New Yorkers how taxes are spent.
newsitem.headline: New website shows New Yorkers how taxes are spent.

text.p: The New York City Independent Budget Office Monday unveiled an interactive website that aims to shows New Yorkers and U.S. taxpayers how their tax dollars are spent by different layers of government.

By plugging in what they paid in federal, state and city taxes from wage-witholding and income tax forms, browsers can breakdown where their taxes went, according to nine general categories that vary a bit for each governmental layer.

New York City residents, for example, can see how much of their taxes paid for police, fire and corrections, while residents throughout the state can see how many of their tax dollars went for law enforcement. All U.S. taxpayers can examine how much they paid in taxes for Social Security and National Defense, among other categories.

Those who do not have access to the Internet website, whose address is www.ibo.nyc.ny.us., can get the same calculations, which the Independent Budget Office calls "income tax receipts," by getting its forms and submitting them to it.
The Independent Budget Office, which was created to serve the same role as the Congressional Budget Office, said it developed the websites to help educate voters.

The exercize does not include how much federal and state aid New York City gets, nor how much federal aid New York State receives, officials with the Independent Budget Office said, explaining this method was chosen to ensure there was no double-counting.

And in some instances, they assumed that New York City funds could be freely shifted around, as is not always the case. "Ultimately, there's one pot of money that's used for all city expenditures," explained Doug Criscitello, director.
